$comment: system-manifest.json — the tracked installation/observation contract (GENERIC-INSTALL-DESIGN.md §3.4). Setup is data-driven from THIS file so the UI, README, and DEPLOY.md can never drift apart: DEPLOY.md's env table is CHECKED against envOverrides below (scripts/check.js), and the /status route reports the same components/ports/health named here. RCOS owns the tested compatibility pin (see COMPAT.md); this file owns install/topology facts.

dsh.pinPolicy: verified-pin (see COMPAT.md) — RCOS owns the known-good pin; upgrades move through verification before it changes

archon.note: The default URL is only the DEFAULT — the configured endpoint comes from archon.baseUrl (env>file>default). The /status archon probe uses the same path the Workflows tab proxies. Mock for sandbox checks lives at scripts/mock-archon.mjs on :13090 (deliberately NOT 3090).

rcos.role: capability + routing + verification architecture (this UI exposes it, never duplicates it)
rcos.install: none — the registry is a FILE the operator points at (registry.path), not a service to install
rcos.health: live read via /status rcos probe: exists + JSON + capabilities[] + declared schema
rcos.schemaPolicy: the public RCOS schema wins (§6 ruling 3) — production divergence is migration debt, not a second truth

operator-ui.role: installation, configuration, observation, intervention surface (this repo)

chrome.role: OPTIONAL local browser binary for the supervised Browser tab only (integration, not core)
chrome.install: install Chrome/Chromium for your OS, or set browser.chromePath

restartSemantics.note: request-time knobs re-resolve per request (restart-free); boot-time knobs are read once in apply() — file changes need a DSH restart. /status exposes both live + configured viewports so drift is visible.

configFile.godConfigRule: operator-ui.config.json contains operator-UI integration/configuration and REFERENCES to authorities (endpoint URLs, file paths, caps, slot names) — never copied DSH/Archon/RCOS state, never secret values (see credentials below)

envOverrides.$comment: Every DSH_OPERATOR_UI_* name the code reads, each naming the config key it wins over. check.js asserts code ⊇ manifest ⊇ DEPLOY.md.

statusRoute.answers: what RCOS pieces are configured, available, missing, invalid, or not yet verified

vocabulary.UNAVAILABLE: configured (or defaulted) but the live probe failed
vocabulary.NOT_CONFIGURED: no value provided where one is required
vocabulary.INVALID: value present but malformed — reported, never a boot failure
vocabulary.UNKNOWN: cannot be known from here — a valid state, never collapsed into one red light

rules: every reported field names its authority (DSH truth from DSH, Archon truth from Archon, registry truth from the registry file; the UI owns only its own integration state)
configuration is separated from observation (a configured URL is not AVAILABLE; an existing path is not valid schema; a populated slot is not VERIFIED)
live authoritative reads/probes per request — nothing cached; each probe carries checkedAt
no secret value can appear (slot names + presence booleans only)
Slice 1 never reports verified:true — Slice 2 owns live verification

credentials.policy: No secrets, ever — not in code, not in screenshots, not in the dev-home. Config carries slot NAMES only (archon.tokenVar names an env var; provider slots name envSlots). Presence checks only, values never read, never reported, never echoed.
credentials.template: fixtures/providers.example.yaml (slot names + REQUIRED/OPTIONAL markers; zeroCredentialProbe names the seed that must verify with NO credentials)

permissions.$comment: Permissions round: presets are operator PERSONALITIES over a lower-level authority contract of scopes (GPT refinement — never four global modes). A capability DECLARES what it requires; the preset pre-authorizes (grants) a subset; the task envelope carries the granted policy it ran (or waits) under. The SAME block renders Preview ('RCOS plans to …') before dispatch and Prove ('RCOS did …' + authority line) after — one vocabulary, two tenses.

presets.PLAN_ONLY: pre-authorizes nothing — every execution needs explicit approval
presets.ASK_BEFORE_ACTION: pre-authorizes read-only-ish scopes (filesystem:read, git:read, browser:read, network:outbound, external:draft); writes/execution/credentials need approval
presets.AUTO_WITHIN_POLICY: pre-authorizes everything except the irreversible/external trio (credentials:use, git:push, external:submit)
presets.FULL_ACCESS: pre-authorizes every listed scope — still bound by capability/runtime safety (seeded + retired capabilities never route; registry still required)

permissions.failClosed: a capability declaring an UNKNOWN scope can never auto-dispatch; PLAN_ONLY pre-authorizes nothing; a missing grant seals an awaiting-approval envelope BEFORE dispatch — nothing executes on a guess
permissions.approval: approval resumes the SAME task (approveTaskId → retryOf + approved flag); the host re-checks the stored envelope is genuinely awaiting-approval first and refuses anything else (409); approval is per task, never a global mode flip
permissions.authorityConfig: authority.preset (env DSH_OPERATOR_UI_AUTHORITY_PRESET > file > default ASK_BEFORE_ACTION) — a preset NAME only, never secrets
permissions.persistence: the granted policy {preset, requires, granted, missing, mode, reason, approvedAt} rides the task envelope in operator-ui/tasks.json — no third store, no new persistence
permissions.faultIsolation: every registered surface is wrapped in an error boundary: a bug may kill its card/surface (rendered as a killed-card fallback), never shell.overlay — the boundary contains, it never rethrows

teachMode.$comment: M2: capability ACQUISITION. Lifecycle GAP → TEACH → BUILD → EVALUATE → CANDIDATE → PROMOTE → ROUTE. THREE identities stay separate and are never mutated into each other: source_task_id (the task whose objective exposed the gap), teaching_task_id (the learning process), capability_id+version (the reusable intelligence IF learning succeeds).
teachMode.hardRule: successful generation does NOT equal learned capability — the candidate is EXECUTED on the real Archon against a held-out deterministic fixture set, and promotion may only be OFFERED when every case passes; a candidate failing any case is refused honestly ('Not added to Intelligence')
teachMode.promotion: always an EXPLICIT human action (Promote to Intelligence); the promoted registry entry carries permanent provenance (builtBy RCOS, sourceTaskId, teachingTaskId, per-case eval run ids, promotedBy operator, promotedAt, version); duplicate-id promotion is refused
teachMode.authority: the candidate DECLARES its required scopes at BUILD time — a learned capability cannot quietly acquire power; unknown scopes fail closed at promotion exactly as at dispatch
teachMode.writes: the ONLY files teaching ever writes: the candidate workflow YAML under teaching.workflowsDir and per-eval fixture files under teaching.workspaceDir (both operator-configured path references); everything durable about the teaching itself lives in tasks.json — no third store
teachMode.honesty: teaching paths unconfigured → the teach action reports NOT_CONFIGURED instead of pretending; eval evidence (expected vs observed totals per case, run ids) is sealed in the teaching envelope

receipt.$comment: SYSTEM-VERIFIED must prove components communicated and executed the verification path (§6 receipt gate): versions, configuration authorities/paths without secrets, health results, execution/result identity, timestamps, hashes/provenance sufficient to reproduce what was tested.

verification.$comment: Slice 2 (VERIFIABLE): turns 'pieces appear healthy' into sealed evidence. Probe B is the REAL RCOS path — routing goes through the configured registry (the seeded capability's workflow binding is read from the registry, never hardcoded) and execution goes through the configured Archon's normal run API. There is no parallel verification architecture to bypass it.
verification.route: POST /plugins/operator-ui/verify (runs probes + writes the receipt) | GET /plugins/operator-ui/verify?op=receipt (read-only freshness verdict)

probes.probeA: verify-machinery — deterministic, zero-credential: manifest load, seed-bundle hashing, config resolution, and an evaluator self-test (accepts the seeded expectation, rejects wrong output and wrong terminal status)
probes.probeB: rcos-execution-path — request → route via configured registry (seeded capability rcos-verify-echo → its `workflow` binding) → execute on configured Archon (POST /api/workflows/{name}/run, same base the Workflows tab proxies) → poll run to terminal → evaluate evidence against the seeded expectation

levels.NOT_VERIFIED: Probe A did not pass — nothing above it may be claimed
levels.SYSTEM_VERIFIED: Probe A passed; Probe B did not run or did not pass (blocker named, never stretched to RCOS_VERIFIED)
levels.RCOS_VERIFIED: Probe A + Probe B both passed — the installation executed the actual RCOS execution path

verification.receiptWrites: the ONLY file this plugin writes, and only on an explicit POST /verify; GET never writes
verification.seal: sha256 over the canonical receipt body without the seal field — a modified body reads TAMPERED, not merely old
verification.staleness: the receipt fingerprints what it tested (node version, manifest sha256, config hash, registry sha256, seed-bundle sha256s); readReceipt recomputes them fresh so a materially different installation reads STALE with reasons
verification.realArchonContract: verified against real Archon v0.10.1 (RC0): catalog entries may be {workflow:{…}}-wrapped (normalized at the proxy/status boundary); dispatch POST /api/workflows/{name}/run requires a conversationId and answers an ACCEPTANCE {accepted:true} — the verifier discovers the new run from the run list; runs need a registered workspace (folder codebase) to execute in
verification.adapterProvenance: the receipt's execution.executionAdapter records what the endpoint itself reported (/api/health version): real Archon reads archon@0.10.1, an unversioned compatible reads archon-compatible (unversioned) — a mock-backed receipt can never pose as a versioned real-Archon one
verification.seedPolicy: seeded/example capabilities are clearly marked (status `seeded`, seed `true`) so they can never be mistaken for accumulated production intelligence; the private workflow library is never bundled
verification.providerNote: provider/model-backed execution is NOT part of the zero-credential seed — provider slots report separately and stay UNVERIFIED unless a live check proves otherwise; they are never a prerequisite for the genesis receipt

goalMode.pipeline: objective → ROUTE (transparent keyword scoring over EVERY registry capability; seeded entries excluded; scores + reasons reported) → EXECUTE (the selected capability's own workflow binding on the configured Archon) → EVIDENCE (terminal poll + node outputs) → VERIFY (M1: a 3-check evaluation gate — terminal status + the registry-declared expectation marker + objective-satisfaction over the evidence text) → SHIP | BLOCK | FAILED
goalMode.taskIdentity: task_id ('goal-xxxxxxxx') is born at goal admission, ABOVE DSH/Archon; attempts are recorded per task; the envelope (route, attempts, checks incl. objective-satisfaction, verdict + scope, trust ladder, next action, lineage) is sealed to operator-ui/tasks.json after every state change — retry = same task new attempt, fork = new task_id with lineage
goalMode.honesty: a capability that declares no expectation can reach COMPLETED but never SHIP; a goal that matches nothing is refused with reasons, never guessed; verdict scope is 'capability-validation' unless the objective-satisfaction check passed ('objective-evaluation') — never silently upgraded
goalMode.persistence: goals are durable in operator-ui/tasks.json (atomic tmp+rename writes; Archon's run record stays the execution truth; restarts lose nothing); the plugin writes only tasks.json + the sealed receipt
